name: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Abī Sāra al-Ruʾāsī
summary: The first Kufan to write a book on grammar, by Thaʿlab's account; nephew of Muʿādh al-Harrāʾ and teacher of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, whom al-Zubaydī puts at the head of the grammarians of Kufa.
bio: Al-Ruʾāsī was Muḥammad ibn Abī Sāra, the nephew of Muʿādh al-Harrāʾ, called al-Ruʾāsī for the size of his head (raʾs). Ibn al-Anbārī cites Ibn Durustawayh that Thaʿlab held him to be the first of the Kufans to write a book on grammar, and that he was the teacher of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ.
Al-Zubaydī opens his list of the grammarians of Kufa with him. His book, called al-Fayṣal, is lost; the later reports say that al-Khalīl asked to see it. The year of his death is not recorded.
uncertain: The story that Sībawayh's 'the Kufan' in the Book is al-Ruʾāsī is told by later writers and disputed.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 65–67
